analysis.title: GS Consumer: Tactical Refresh
key_insights: The Retail group rose 5.5% on 11/4, its biggest 1-day move in the last year. That was +390 bps versus SPY, the 2nd largest 1-day outperformance in the last 2 years.
XRT is at 5-year highs and XLP (Staples) is at all-time highs.

Investor conviction in the consumer rally is low. Most inbound requests from meetings in NYC and Boston have been some version of 'what can I fade?', concentrated in Staples but also present in Discretionary.
The chase has not happened. Both the GS high touch desk and PB desk have not seen an aggressive move to get long the space at the single stock level.
Discretionary and Staples are at multi-year lows as a percentage of the total GS PB book, and long/short ratios have barely moved off the lows.
The ETF highs look macro/rotational rather than single-name fundamental buying. Supply has largely dried up, a change from the summer and early September period.

Thematic interest in the last couple of sessions centered on low-income consumer exposure. The stated drivers are a debate over whether SNAP and Medicaid headwinds could ease in mid-2027 around debt limit negotiations, and easing oil prices.
Single names most discussed in meetings: TPR, VIK/RCL, ONON, DG, MCD, WING, PEP, TJX/BURL.
Feiler describes consumer fundamentals as 'fine' or resilient, with winners and losers underneath.

The GS Macro US Consumer dashboard published two weeks earlier is titled 'Resilience'. GS Macro forecasts near-potential spending growth in 2027 and real income growth acceleration in 2027, particularly for the lowest income consumers.

sector_views.rationale: Retail group had its biggest 1-day move in a year and XRT is at 5-year highs, but long/short ratios and PB book share remain near multi-year lows, so positioning shows no chase. Feiler describes fundamentals as fine.
XLP is at all-time highs and is the main focus of 'what can I fade?' requests. PB book share and long/short ratios are near lows, and the rally looks macro/rotational.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS Macro is less concerned about a significant slowdown in spending growth given its continued resilience.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS Macro's base case macro outlook supports consumer spending resilience.

SNAP and Medicaid headwinds for low-income consumers could persist, with possible easing in mid-2027 tied to debt limit negotiations.
